messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Tamil, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Tamil line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
நான் கீழ் இடத்திற்கு விழுந்து கொண்டிருந்தபோது, என் கண்களின் முன்னால் ஒன்று தோன்றியது நீண்ட அமைதியின் மூலம் அது குரல் மங்கியதாகத் தோன்றியது.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

**Word‑to‑Tamil Mapping Table**
| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Tamil) | Back‑Translation (English) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------|--------| | Mentre | temporal subordinator “while” | **கொண்டிருந்தபோது** | “while (… was happening)” | OK | | ch'i' | 1st sg pronoun “I” (contraction of *che io*) | **நான்** | “I” | OK | | rovinava | imperfect verb “was falling / going down” | **விழுந்து** | “fell” (verb root) | OK | | in | preposition “to / toward” | **இடத்திற்கு** | “to the place” | OK | | basso | adjective “low” | **கீழ்** | “low / down” | OK | | loco | noun “place, location” | **இடத்திற்கு** | “to the place” | OK | | dinanzi | adverb/preposition “before, in front of” | **முன்னால்** | “before / in front of” | OK | | a | preposition linking “dinanzi” to the noun phrase | *(none needed in Tamil)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | li | definite article “the” (masc. plural) | *(none needed in Tamil)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | occhi | noun “eyes” | **கண்களின்** | “eyes (genitive)” | OK | | mi | 1st sg dative “to me / my” | **என்** | “my” (possessive) | OK | | si | reflexive/impersonal pronoun used in passive | *(none needed in Tamil)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | fu | auxiliary verb “was” (past remote) | *(none needed in Tamil)* | – | UNNECESSARY | | offerto | past participle “offered / presented” | **தோன்றியது** | “appeared / was shown” | OK | | chi | relative pronoun “one who / who” | **அது** | “it / that one” | OK | | per | preposition “through / by means of” | **மூலம்** | “by means of” | OK | | lungo | adjective “long” | **நீண்ட** | “long” | OK | | silenzio | noun “silence” | **அமைதியின்** | “of silence” (genitive) | OK | | parea | verb “seemed” | **தோன்றியது** | “seemed / appeared” | OK | | fioco | adjective “hoarse / weak” | **மங்கியதாகத்** | “as being hoarse / faint” | OK |
---
### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: `a`, `li`, `si`, `fu` – these grammatical particles have no direct counterpart in Tamil and are naturally omitted. - No **MISSING**, **WRONG**, or **GRAMMAR** issues were found; all essential meanings are represented in the Tamil rendering.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Tamil script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Tamil text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
